about: The Foundation's security and privacy risk assessment as authored analysis: the threat sources (NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 Table D-2, with D-3 to D-5 adversary characteristics), the data-flow elements of the Foundation's systems, every STRIDE category each element is open to and every LINDDUN category each element carrying personal data is open to (answered by a threat event or stated open, never both), the threat events (Appendix E) with their ATT&CK and ATLAS techniques and G-2/G-3, G-4 and H-3 levels, the controls with the NIST CSF 2.0 outcomes they achieve and the evidence for them, the CSF 2.0 outcomes no control achieves, and the claims this assessment could not settle. security/project.mjs resolves every reference against the pinned standards in security/sources.json and computes overall likelihood (Table G-5) and risk (Table I-2) from the tables it reads from the publication; nothing here states a risk level. Levels are SP 800-30's qualitative scale: VL, L, M, H, VH. A control's status is OSCAL 1.1 implementation-status: implemented, partial, planned, alternative, not-applicable.
mission: The UOR Foundation is a nonprofit that implements, maintains and publishes the UOR Framework and Prism as free public-benefit services and resources, for the democratization of technology. Its work is public by design: every repository, proof, corpus and decision record is published, its development is driven by AI agents acting for its maintainers, and its novel claims draw public scrutiny.

sources.name: Opportunistic outsider
sources.text: Spammers, scammers and drive-by attackers who find the Foundation's public repositories, CI, website and Discord through search and automation.

sources.name: Software supply chain attackers
sources.text: Groups that compromise maintainers, CI actions, packages and registries to reach every downstream user, as in the 2025 tj-actions and npm package-worm incidents. The Foundation's SDK images and crates are pinned by every Prism project, so they are a multiplier target.

sources.name: Hostile scrutinizer
sources.text: Individuals drawn by the Foundation's public novel claims who seek to discredit, misrepresent, harass or deanonymize the Foundation and its people, using everything the Foundation publishes.

sources.name: Crypto and impersonation scam operators
sources.text: Ad hoc groups that impersonate open-source foundations and their maintainers on Discord, lookalike domains and repositories to defraud members, drawn by crypto-adjacent names in the ecosystem.

sources.name: State-sponsored actor
sources.text: A state actor with interest in addressing, verification and AI-assurance technology. No observation in this assessment points to one; the source is recorded so that Table D-2 is answered in full.

sources.name: Instructed agent
sources.text: An AI agent acting with a maintainer's credentials whose instructions an outsider controls through text it reads: an issue, a pull request, a comment, a Discord message or a fetched page.

sources.name: Maintainer or agent error
sources.text: A maintainer, or an agent acting for one, who misconfigures an organization setting, ruleset, workflow or data store, as on 2026-11-14 when the first rulesets blocked pull requests organization-wide.

sources.name: Upstream software defect
sources.text: A defect in software the Foundation runs, such as the credential leak in Perceval archives the Foundation found and reported in November 2026.

sources.name: Provider outage or account action
sources.text: An outage of, or an account action by, GitHub, Discord, Supabase, Lovable or the domain registrar, on which every Foundation service depends.

elements.name: Contributor
elements.text: A person outside the maintainers who opens an issue or pull request.

elements.name: Maintainer
elements.text: An Organization Owner or Maintainer under GOVERNANCE.md, whose GitHub account holds the organization's administrative rights.

elements.name: AI agent
elements.text: Claude, Cursor, Lovable and other agents that commit and act as a maintainer's delegate (W3C PROV-O actedOnBehalfOf, governance/agents.json).

elements.name: Discord member
elements.text: A member of the Foundation's Discord guild.

stride.R: open: Discord keeps every message under the member's account, and no Foundation decision rests on a member's statement.

elements.name: Website visitor
elements.text: A person using uor.foundation, signed in or not.

stride.R: open: no Foundation decision rests on a visitor's act; Supabase Auth keeps its own record of account events (open claim OC-AUTHLOG).

linddun.Nr: open: the website records no statement a visitor could later need to deny.
linddun.De: open: the website's public pages do not reveal whether a given person holds an account.

elements.name: Upstream supplier
elements.text: GitHub Actions authors, crate and npm registries, CHAOSS and other upstream projects the Foundation's builds read.

stride.R: open: every upstream input is pinned by commit or digest, so what a supplier supplied is fixed by its address.

elements.name: Public and press
elements.text: Anyone reading the Foundation's claims, including people scrutinizing them.

elements.name: GitHub organization and CI
elements.text: The UOR-Foundation organization's repositories, rulesets and GitHub Actions, including the merge controller and the apply-settings run.

elements.name: Agent loop
elements.text: Claude sessions and the scheduled agent task that read issues, pull requests, CI output and Discord and push as a maintainer.

stride.D: open: the loop serves no one outside the Foundation; when it stops, work waits and nothing is exposed.

elements.name: Website
elements.text: The uor.foundation single-page application built from UOR-Foundation/website, including commits Lovable makes to it.

elements.name: Supabase backend
elements.text: The Supabase project behind the website: Auth, PostgREST over Postgres, storage and edge functions.

stride.R: open: Supabase keeps the API and Auth logs, which this assessment has not read (open claim OC-AUTHLOG).

linddun.Nr: open: the backend records no act a person could later need to deny beyond what they themselves store.

elements.name: Discord guild and Foundation bot
elements.text: The Foundation's Discord guild, its moderation, and the read-only bot that the discord-live and observation runs use.

stride.R: open: Discord's audit log records every moderator act, which this assessment has not read (open claim OC-DISCORDMOD).

elements.name: Release pipeline
elements.text: The runs that publish SDK images to ghcr.io, crates, npm packages and GitHub Pages sites.

elements.name: Git repositories
elements.text: The 31 public repositories of the ecosystem register, the Foundation's source of truth.

elements.name: Actions secrets
elements.text: ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN and the other repository secrets.

stride.R: open: GitHub's organization audit log records every secret change; agent sessions cannot read it (open claim OC-AUDITLOG).

elements.name: Supabase database
elements.text: The website's Postgres: 87 tables, among them contacts, calendar events, AI conversations, agent memories and encrypted messages.

stride.R: open: Supabase keeps the database's own logs, which this assessment has not read (open claim OC-AUTHLOG).

linddun.Nr: open: what a person stores is theirs; the database keeps no record of them beyond it.

elements.name: Published corpora
elements.text: The GrimoireLab observation corpus, the recorded Discord responses and the telemetry branch, in the public community repository.

elements.name: Container registry
elements.text: The PrismPM SDK images on ghcr.io that every Prism project pins by digest.

stride.I: open: the SDK images are public by design and hold no secret.

elements.name: Discord message history
elements.text: The guild's messages as Discord stores them.

stride.R: open: Discord's audit log records message deletions by moderators and bots (open claim OC-DISCORDMOD).

elements.name: Domains and DNS
elements.text: uor.foundation, its subdomains and their DNS records at the registrar.

stride.R: open: the registrar keeps the record of every change to the registration and zone (open claim OC-DOMAIN).
stride.I: open: DNS records are public by design.

elements.name: Package namespaces
elements.text: The crate, npm, PyPI and container names the Foundation publishes under or tells people to install, including names it has not claimed.

stride.I: open: package names and metadata are public by design.

elements.name: Contribution
elements.text: An issue or pull request from a contributor into a repository and its CI.

stride.I: open: issues and pull requests are public by design.

elements.name: Agent push
elements.text: Commits, pull requests and comments an agent makes as a maintainer.

elements.name: Secret use
elements.text: A workflow run reading a secret and calling an API with it.

elements.name: Corpus publication
elements.text: A collection run writing Discord and GitHub activity into the public corpus.

elements.name: Website traffic
elements.text: HTTPS between a visitor's browser and the website.

elements.name: Website data access
elements.text: supabase-js calls from the browser to the Supabase API with the publishable key and a user session.

linddun.Nr: open: a call records nothing a person could need to deny beyond what they store.

elements.name: Upstream inputs
elements.text: Actions, crates, packages and images a build fetches.

stride.I: open: the inputs are public packages.

elements.name: Release publication
elements.text: A release run pushing an image or package to a registry.

elements.name: Discord conversation
elements.text: Messages and direct messages between members, maintainers and the bot.

elements.name: Untrusted text to agents
elements.text: Issue, pull request, comment, CI log, web page and Discord text an agent reads as input.

threats.name: Maintainer account takeover
threats.text: A maintainer's GitHub account is phished or its session stolen, and the attacker changes rulesets, secrets or code with organization-owner rights.

threats.name: Poisoned pipeline execution
threats.text: A pull request from a fork runs attacker code in a privileged workflow (pull_request_target, workflow_run or script injection) and gains its token or secrets.

threats.name: Compromised action or dependency
threats.text: A third-party GitHub Action, crate or npm package the builds fetch is replaced with a malicious version.

threats.name: Secret exfiltration from CI
threats.text: A workflow, action or log leaks ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN or a webhook URL; ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN can rewrite every repository's settings.

threats.name: Agent prompt injection
threats.text: Text an agent reads (an issue, a comment, a CI log, a page, a Discord message) instructs it, and it pushes, comments, posts or discloses with the maintainer's credentials.

threats.name: Unattributable agent acts
threats.text: Agents push as a maintainer's account, so a commit, review or setting change cannot be told apart from the maintainer's own without the delegation record.

threats.name: Discord impersonation and scam messages
threats.text: Accounts posing as maintainers, support or the Foundation message members with fake airdrops, tokens, jobs or verification links.

threats.name: Discord bot token compromise
threats.text: The Foundation bot's token leaks, and its holder reads every channel the bot can see or acts as the bot.

threats.name: Re-identification of published community activity
threats.text: The public corpus keeps Discord message and channel ids, times and an unsalted sha256 of each Discord user id. Anyone in the guild can open a message id and see its author, and anyone with a user id can compute its pseudonym, so every member's activity timeline is linkable and identifiable (LINDDUN Linking, Identifying, Detecting).

threats.name: Website data store exposure
threats.text: A missing or permissive row-level security policy lets anyone with the publishable key read or write personal data in the Supabase tables.

threats.name: Website tampering through an integration
threats.text: An integration with write access to the website repository (Lovable's app, an agent) is compromised or misled and publishes altered content or code.

threats.name: Domain hijack or lookalike domain
threats.text: uor.foundation's registration or DNS is taken over, or a lookalike domain serves a fake Foundation site.

threats.name: Tampered SDK image or release
threats.text: A published SDK image or package is replaced or a malicious one is published under the Foundation's name; every Prism project builds through the SDK. The community and foundry repositories pin the SDK image from the personal ghcr.io/afflom namespace, so the release identity is one person's account.

threats.name: Credentials in tool archives
threats.text: Perceval archives pickle the HTTP response with its request headers, so an archive shared for replay carries the token that fetched it (found by the Foundation in 15 backends at 1.6.2, reported to CHAOSS on 2026-11-14).

threats.name: CI resource abuse
threats.text: Fork pull requests or comment triggers run cryptominers or exhaust Actions minutes and agent time.

threats.name: Discord raid or spam flood
threats.text: A burst of new accounts joins and floods channels with spam or harassment.

threats.name: Organization misconfiguration
threats.text: A ruleset, workflow or setting change by a maintainer or agent blocks work or weakens a control across the organization.

threats.name: Repository loss
threats.text: Repositories, history or the organization itself are deleted, force-pushed or suspended.

threats.name: Provider outage or suspension
threats.text: GitHub, Discord, Supabase, Lovable or the registrar is down or acts on the Foundation's account.

threats.name: Impersonation of the Foundation and misrepresented claims
threats.text: Lookalike accounts, repositories or tokens speak as the Foundation, or the Foundation's claims are restated as more or less than its evidence shows, and a reader cannot check which statement is the Foundation's.

threats.name: Malicious contribution
threats.text: A contributor, possibly after building trust over time, lands a backdoor or weakened gate in a pull request.

threats.name: Reconnaissance of public repositories
threats.rationale: Publishing everything is the mission; what reconnaissance reads is public by design, and no secret is kept in a repository (Scorecard and secret scanning check that).
threats.text: Automated clients clone and scrape the repositories and site to map the Foundation's people, systems and dependencies.

threats.name: Website account attacks
threats.text: Password spraying or credential stuffing against Supabase Auth sign-in.

threats.name: Traffic interception
threats.text: A network attacker reads or alters website or API traffic.

threats.name: Forged or repudiated authorship
threats.text: Git author fields are free text, so an unsigned commit can claim any author, and an author can deny an unsigned commit.

threats.name: Website denial of service
threats.text: Floods make the website or its backend unavailable.

threats.name: Falsified measurement corpus
threats.text: The published corpus or telemetry is altered to change the Foundation's community metrics.

threats.name: Members unaware of measurement
threats.text: Discord members are not told that their activity metadata is collected, pseudonymized and published, or how to object (LINDDUN Unawareness and Unintervenability).

threats.name: Privacy obligations not documented
threats.text: The website and Discord process personal data of people in many jurisdictions, and no privacy notice states the purposes, lawful basis, retention or data-subject rights (LINDDUN Non-compliance).

threats.name: Deleted activity retained
threats.text: The corpus keeps the ids and times of messages a member later deletes, so the member cannot withdraw them (LINDDUN Non-repudiation).

threats.name: Domain registration lapse
threats.text: uor.foundation expires on 2027-01-21 (observed 2026-11-15 by the asset register); if it lapses, anyone can register it and receive the Foundation's mail, links and install instructions.

threats.name: Name squatting and dependency confusion
threats.text: Install names the website tells people to use (crates.io prism-code, PyPI prism-code, npm @uor/prism) are unclaimed, and private crate names in compression (figures, frontier) are already taken on crates.io by other publishers, so an install or build can fetch someone else's package.

threats.name: Credentials committed to a public repository
threats.text: The website repository commits .env (a Supabase publishable key, public by design) and a DocsGPT agent API key in src/docsgpt.ts, which anyone can use against the Foundation's DocsGPT quota.

threats.name: Subdomain takeover
threats.text: app.uor.foundation and schemas.uor.foundation are referenced but do not resolve; a record later pointed at a third-party service the Foundation does not hold could be claimed by someone else.

controls.name: Two-factor authentication for every member
controls.text: GitHub accounts with organization rights use phishing-resistant two-factor authentication. Whether the organization requires it is open claim OC-2FA.

controls.name: Repository rulesets
controls.text: Every repository's default branch requires a pull request and passing checks and blocks force-pushes and deletion, applied by apply-settings from the remediation register.

controls.name: Human gates on the merge controller
controls.text: Outside, secrets, trust-root and shared-repository changes (H1 to H4) need a human; the controller decides with a proved XACML policy.

controls.name: No privileged workflow runs fork code
controls.text: No workflow checks out fork code under pull_request_target or workflow_run, or interpolates untrusted event text into a script. Scorecard's Dangerous-Workflow check measures it on every repository.

controls.name: Least-privilege workflow tokens
controls.text: Workflows declare read-only top-level permissions and do not persist checkout credentials.

controls.name: Fork pull request approval
controls.text: Workflows from first-time contributors' forks wait for a maintainer's approval before they run; the organization setting is open claim OC-FORKAPPROVAL.

controls.name: Actions pinned by commit
controls.text: Every third-party action is pinned by full commit SHA; Scorecard's Pinned-Dependencies check measures it.

controls.name: Locked production dependencies
controls.text: AGENTS.md R6: shipped outputs use only locked production dependencies; cargo-deny checks licenses, sources and advisories.

controls.name: Dependency update and vulnerability alerts
controls.text: Dependency updates and known-vulnerability alerts are raised for every repository; Scorecard measures both.

controls.name: Secrets confined to gated runs
controls.text: A diff that touches a secret reference is decided as H2 and needs a human; ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN is read only by the label-triggered apply-settings job.

controls.name: Secret scanning and push protection
controls.text: GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled on every repository; the setting is open claim OC-SECRETSCAN.

controls.name: Fetched text is data, never instructions
controls.text: Agents treat issue, comment, CI, page and Discord text as data and act only on their maintainer's own words; the agent loop never skips a check or touches H1 to H3.

controls.name: Proved gates on every merge
controls.text: Every merge passes just vv in the pinned SDK, with Lean-checked models and planted-defect gates, so an injected or malicious change must also defeat the proofs.

controls.name: People-reach gate
controls.text: Any act a contributor, participant or partner would see is denied unless Alex approves that exact act.

controls.name: Agent delegation record
controls.text: Each agent is a Schema.org SoftwareApplication with a PROV-O actedOnBehalfOf delegation to the person it works for, read from Co-Authored-By trailers.

controls.name: Decision telemetry
controls.text: Every automated decision is a CloudEvents 1.0 record in the run's artifact and job summary.

controls.name: Discord moderation and verification
controls.text: The Code of Conduct enforcement ladder is a proved decision app; the guild's verification level and AutoMod rules are open claim OC-DISCORDMOD, and the corpus holds no AutoMod action (message type 24).

controls.name: Official channels statement
controls.text: A published list of the Foundation's official accounts, domains and the fact that the Foundation never sends direct messages asking for keys, payments or sign-ins.

controls.name: Least-privilege bot
controls.text: The bot reads only the channels the proved discord-read app permits and holds no moderation rights.

controls.name: Corpus minimization
controls.text: The corpus drops message text, names, emails and thread titles; it still keeps message ids and an unsalted user-id hash (T09).

controls.name: Keyed pseudonyms and aggregate publication
controls.text: Publish Discord activity only as aggregates, or replace ids and hashes with keyed pseudonyms (ISO/IEC 20889) whose key never leaves the collection run, and honor deletions in the next collection.

controls.name: Row-level security on every table
controls.text: Open and signed-in-only policies were removed on 2026-11-12; the full policy set lives only in the Supabase project (open claim OC-RLS).

controls.name: Supabase database linter
controls.text: Run Supabase's own linter (splinter) against the database on every migration; it is the oracle for row-level security and exposed functions.

controls.name: Integration access review
controls.text: Review the GitHub Apps and integrations installed on the organization and the website repository, and grant each only the repositories it needs.

controls.name: Domain protection
controls.text: Registrar lock, DNSSEC and CAA records for uor.foundation; the current state is open claim OC-DOMAIN.

controls.name: Digest-pinned SDK
controls.text: Every Prism project selects the SDK by image digest, so a replaced tag changes nothing it builds.

controls.name: Signed releases with provenance
controls.text: Releases and images carry signatures and build provenance; Scorecard's Signed-Releases and Packaging checks measure it.

controls.name: Archive credential audit
controls.text: The Discord backend strips Authorization before archiving, the leak audit runs over upstream's own archive tests, and the finding was reported to CHAOSS privately.

controls.name: Path-filtered, cancellable CI
controls.text: Workflows filter by path, reuse results by content address and cancel superseded runs.

controls.name: Settings applied from a reviewed register
controls.text: Organization settings change only through apply-settings, which dry-runs on every pull request and stops on any failed read.

controls.name: Off-platform repository backup
controls.text: Mirror every repository's history and the published corpora outside GitHub, and test a restore.

controls.name: Reproducible, content-addressed builds
controls.text: Every output is rebuilt from pinned inputs to the same bytes, so a service can be restored on another host and checked by its address.

controls.name: Claims at their evidence level
controls.text: AGENTS.md R2: every claim is published as imported, built or open, with the proof or measurement behind it, so anyone can check what the Foundation actually claims.

controls.name: Code owners and review
controls.text: GOVERNANCE.md 6.2 review, with the controller reviewing as the Owner's agent; Scorecard's Code-Review check measures it.

controls.name: Auth rate limits and leaked-password protection
controls.text: Supabase Auth rate limits, CAPTCHA and leaked-password protection; the project's settings are open claim OC-AUTHLOG.

controls.name: HTTPS with HSTS
controls.text: The site and Supabase API are served only over HTTPS; HSTS preload is not established.

controls.name: Signed commits
controls.text: Require verified signatures on default branches and sign agent commits with a key bound to the delegation.

controls.name: Digest-pinned corpus with replay
controls.text: Every corpus file is pinned by sha256 and replay re-derives it from the recorded responses.

controls.name: Privacy notice
controls.text: A privacy notice for the website and Discord measurement: purposes, lawful basis, retention, data-subject rights and how to object, in the Discord rules channel and on the site.

controls.name: Vulnerability disclosure policy
controls.text: SECURITY.md sets private reporting, response timelines and a post-incident review; the site publishes no RFC 9116 security.txt.

controls.name: This security model
controls.text: This register: the mission, the data flows, the threat sources and events with their ATT&CK and ATLAS techniques, risk computed by SP 800-30, and the response chosen for each.

controls.name: Telemetry review
controls.text: Traffic, clone, fork and workflow telemetry is collected and compared with the Foundation's own activity, so what remains is visible; the organization audit log is not yet read (OC-AUDITLOG).

controls.name: Governance and roles
controls.text: The Bylaws and GOVERNANCE.md name the Board, the Organization Owner, Maintainers and the TOC, projected into Foundation.Governance.V1.

controls.name: Emergency and hotfix procedure
controls.text: GOVERNANCE.md 7.4 sets the emergency procedure and SECURITY.md the remediation, release, disclosure and review steps; no incident response plan beyond them names roles, criteria or exercises.

controls.name: Repository standards and inventory
controls.text: Every public repository is registered with its tier, status and lifecycle, and archived or folded when it ends.

controls.name: Static analysis
controls.text: CodeQL or an equivalent runs on every pull request; Scorecard's SAST check measures it.

controls.name: Domain renewal and ownership record
controls.text: Auto-renewal with a recorded expiry, held by the Foundation's registrar account with more than one owner.

controls.name: Claim every published name
controls.text: Register every crate, npm and PyPI name the Foundation documents, rename private crates whose names others hold, and resolve private dependencies only from the Foundation's own sources.

controls.name: Rotate and move the exposed key
controls.text: Rotate the DocsGPT key and serve it through a server-side proxy with a rate limit; keep .env out of the repository except for public values.

controls.name: Publish the SDK from the organization namespace
controls.text: Publish and pin the SDK image under ghcr.io/uor-foundation, with more than one owner, so no release depends on a personal account.

controls.name: No dangling DNS
controls.text: Review every DNS record for targets the Foundation does not hold, and create a referenced subdomain only together with the service it points at.

gaps.GV.RM-01: planned: the Board has not adopted security risk management objectives.
gaps.GV.RM-02: planned: no risk appetite or tolerance statement; this model's accept responses are its first draft.
gaps.GV.RM-03: planned: the Foundation has no enterprise risk register beyond this model.
gaps.GV.RM-04: planned: the SP 800-39 response options this model uses are not adopted as policy.
gaps.GV.RM-05: planned: security reporting lines to the Board are not established.
gaps.GV.RM-07: planned: positive risks are not characterized.
gaps.GV.RR-03: planned: no resources are allocated to security.
gaps.GV.RR-04: not-applicable: the Foundation has no employees; contributors are volunteers and agents.
gaps.GV.OV-01: planned: no strategy review is scheduled.
gaps.GV.OV-02: planned: no strategy review is scheduled.
gaps.GV.OV-03: planned: no performance review is scheduled.
gaps.GV.SC-01: planned: no supply chain risk management program.
gaps.GV.SC-03: planned: supply chain risk is not part of risk management beyond this model.
gaps.GV.SC-05: planned: no supplier agreement carries security requirements.
gaps.GV.SC-06: planned: no due diligence before a new integration.
gaps.GV.SC-08: planned: suppliers are not part of incident planning.
gaps.GV.SC-10: planned: no off-boarding provision for integrations.
gaps.ID.AM-01: not-applicable: the Foundation manages no hardware; every service is hosted by a provider.
gaps.ID.AM-04: planned: the inventory of supplier services comes with the Foundation asset register.
gaps.ID.RA-10: planned: critical suppliers are not assessed before use.
gaps.ID.IM-03: planned: improvements from operations are not yet drawn from the decision telemetry.
gaps.PR.AA-06: not-applicable: the Foundation has no physical premises or hardware.
gaps.PR.AT-01: planned: no security awareness for contributors.
gaps.PR.DS-10: planned: data in use is not protected beyond the providers' own controls.
gaps.PR.PS-03: not-applicable: the Foundation manages no hardware.
gaps.PR.IR-01: planned: the Supabase project's network restrictions are not established.
gaps.PR.IR-02: not-applicable: the Foundation operates no equipment exposed to environmental threats.
gaps.DE.CM-02: not-applicable: the Foundation has no physical environment.
gaps.DE.AE-04: planned: no method estimates an adverse event's impact and scope.
gaps.DE.AE-06: planned: no alert reaches a maintainer when telemetry shows an adverse event.
gaps.DE.AE-08: planned: no incident criteria are defined.
gaps.RS.MA-05: planned: no recovery criteria are defined.
gaps.RS.AN-08: planned: no method estimates an incident's magnitude.
gaps.RC.RP-04: planned: post-incident norms are not set.
gaps.RC.RP-06: planned: no criteria declare the end of recovery.
gaps.RC.CO-03: planned: recovery communication is not set.

openClaims.subject: GitHub organization
openClaims.detail: Whether the organization requires two-factor authentication, and of which kind. Agent sessions cannot read organization settings.

openClaims.subject: GitHub organization
openClaims.detail: The organization audit log (sign-ins, secret and setting changes, app installs). The API path is closed to agent sessions.

openClaims.subject: GitHub organization
openClaims.detail: Whether secret scanning and push protection are on for every repository.

openClaims.subject: GitHub organization
openClaims.detail: The setting that decides when fork pull request workflows need approval.

openClaims.subject: Supabase project
openClaims.detail: The live row-level security policies of the website's 87 tables; the repository holds only two migrations.

openClaims.subject: Supabase project
openClaims.detail: Supabase Auth settings (rate limits, CAPTCHA, leaked-password protection) and its API and Auth logs.

openClaims.subject: Discord guild
openClaims.detail: The guild's verification level, AutoMod rules, moderator roles and audit log.

openClaims.subject: uor.foundation
openClaims.detail: Registrar lock, DNSSEC, CAA and who holds the registrar account.

openClaims.subject: GitHub traffic
openClaims.detail: Who makes the clones that the Foundation's own Actions jobs do not explain. GitHub reports counts, not clients; agent sessions, Lovable's sync and mirrors also clone, and none of them is counted here.

openClaims.subject: Public scrutiny
openClaims.detail: Influence and disinformation campaigns against the Foundation's claims. ATT&CK does not cover them; a catalog that does (DISARM) is not yet pinned.
